1.name: Fuselage
1.note: Thin skins riveted to frames act as one shell: the wing, tail, engine mount and landing gear all hang their loads on it.

2.name: Wing
2.note: Makes the lift, L = ½ρV²S·C_L. The front spar carries the bending; ribs and skin hold the aerofoil's shape.

3.name: Wing strut
3.note: Braces each wing to the fuselage so the spar can be light. In flight it is in tension, carrying part of the lift down to the cabin floor.

4.name: Fin and tailplane
4.note: The feathers of the arrow: the tailplane keeps the nose steady in pitch and the fin in yaw, so the aeroplane flies straight on its own.

5.name: Engine
5.note: Air-cooled and carburetted, it turns the propeller directly with no gearbox. Two magnetos fire two plugs in every cylinder.

6.name: Propeller
6.spec: Ø1905 mm, two blades, fixed pitch
6.note: A rotating wing: each blade's lift, pointed forward, is the thrust. Fixed pitch means one blade angle, a compromise between climb and cruise.

7.name: Engine mount
7.note: Hangs the engine off the firewall on rubber bushes and carries the nose gear; thrust, weight and torque all pass through it.

8.name: Cowling
8.note: Streamlines the engine and guides the cooling air over the cylinder fins and out at the bottom.

9.name: Fuel tank
9.note: Sits between the spars, above the engine, so fuel falls to the carburettor by gravity alone: no pump is needed.

10.name: Control wheel and cables
10.note: Push or pull the wheel for the elevator, turn it for the ailerons; cables over pulleys carry the movement out to every surface.

11.name: Aileron
11.note: One goes up, the other down, so the wings lift unequally and the aeroplane rolls. The larger up-throw reduces adverse yaw.

12.name: Elevator
12.note: Sets the angle of attack, and in steady flight that sets the airspeed: pull for more α and less speed, push for the reverse.

13.name: Rudder
13.note: Yaws the nose. It does not turn the aeroplane; it keeps the turn coordinated by cancelling the ailerons' adverse yaw.

14.name: Flap
14.note: Adds camber and opens a slot, raising C_L,max: at full weight the stall falls from 53 to 48 kt, so the aeroplane can land slower.

15.name: Main gear
15.note: One tapered spring bar per side soaks up the landing with no oil and no joints; hydraulic disc brakes stop the wheels.

16.name: Nose gear
16.note: An air-oil strut cushions the nose. The rudder pedals steer it on the ground, and a damper stops the wheel shimmying.

17.name: Pitot head
17.note: Faces the airflow to sense total pressure; the airspeed indicator subtracts static pressure, and what is left, ½ρV², is airspeed.

18.name: Instrument panel
18.note: Airspeed, attitude, altitude, turn, heading and climb. The attitude and heading gyros spin on air drawn by the vacuum pump.

19.name: Battery
19.note: Starts the engine and backs up the alternator. The master switch connects it to the bus, and a breaker guards every circuit.

20.name: Seat
20.note: Where people sit moves the centre of gravity: the front seats sit almost on the CG range, the rear bench pulls it aft toward FS 1201.

21.name: Windscreen and windows
21.note: Big windows under a high wing give a clear view down. Acrylic is light, tough and easy to form.
